deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 69-71). Grothendieck compares two cohomologies of a scheme X over a base S, essentially in characteristic 0. The first is crystalline (here effectively infinitesimal) cohomology H*(X_cris, F). The second is the cohomology of the 'stratified' (stratifying) site/topos H*(X_strat, F), whose coefficients are modules with stratification, i.e. Grothendieck-style infinite-order connections. The previous page proves the comparison for O_X when X embeds in a smooth Y over C. It goes through Hartshorne-style algebraic de Rham cohomology on the formal completion, the analytic comparison H*(X^an, Ω^._formal) = H*(X^an, C), and passage to the limit over infinitesimal neighbourhoods Y(i). It then states the general problem: for X locally of finite presentation over S and F satisfying the usual hypotheses, is H*(X_cris, F) -> H*(X_strat, F) an isomorphism?

This page reformulates that problem. Let X be as above, X_0 -> X a nilpotent immersion and Y of finite presentation over S. Then the conjecture is equivalent to the isomorphism H^q(X_strat, F) ≅ H^q(X_0,strat, F), i.e. nilpotent invariance of stratified cohomology. One may moreover assume S, X, X_0 affine. The reasoning is that crystalline/infinitesimal cohomology is insensitive to nilpotent immersions: in characteristic 0 the topoi of X and X_0 coincide. So the comparison 'cris = strat' holds if and only if the stratified side has the same invariance, given that the comparison holds for smooth objects, where both sides compute de Rham cohomology. Reduction to affines is by Mayer-Vietoris / descent.

The Remark: for S = Spec k with k a complete non-archimedean valued field, one should ask whether the conjecture holds for analytic spaces over k. He first wrote 'Tate rigid-analytic spaces' and 'rigides', crossed these out, and replaced them with 'espaces analytiques "flasques"' (scare quotes). He then notes that this gives no remarkable global information ('Mais cela n'amène pas d'indications globales si remarquables...'). The notebook breaks off here.
errors: The equivalence is asserted, not proved. It tacitly uses (i) nilpotent invariance of the crystalline/infinitesimal topos, which is valid in characteristic 0 or with PD hypotheses, not in general, and (ii) validity of the comparison in the smooth case. In characteristic p, stratified cohomology (of HPD/stratified modules) and crystalline cohomology genuinely differ, so the 'hypothèses habituelles' must include characteristic-0 or analogous assumptions.

The reading of the subscript (strat vs fl) and of the object 'Y de prés. finie' is uncertain. If the subscript were 'fl' (flat site), the statement would be false in general, so 'strat' is the only sensible reading.

ideas.what: Reduction of the crystalline-vs-stratified comparison conjecture to nilpotent invariance of stratified cohomology, with reduction to the affine case
ideas.modern_name: Nilpotent (topological) invariance of infinitesimal/de Rham-type cohomology; comparison of infinitesimal cohomology with cohomology of D-modules / stratified modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck ('Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', IHES 1966 / Dix exposés 1968); Berthelot (1974)
ideas.where_published: Related material in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968); this exact equivalence is unsure

ideas.what: Asking whether the crystalline/infinitesimal = stratified comparison holds for non-archimedean analytic spaces, replacing Tate rigid spaces by some class of 'flasque' analytic spaces
ideas.modern_name: Infinitesimal/de Rham cohomology of rigid-analytic spaces; overconvergent (dagger) spaces as the right setting for de Rham comparison
ideas.usually_credited_to: Monsky–Washnitzer (1968), Berthelot (rigid cohomology, 1980s-90s), Grosse-Klönne (dagger spaces, 2000), H. Guo (infinitesimal cohomology of rigid spaces, ~2019-21)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes testing the crystalline/infinitesimal vs stratified comparison for non-archimedean analytic spaces. He explicitly abandons Tate rigid spaces in favour of an unspecified class of 'flasque' analytic spaces, foreshadowing the later realisation that rigid de Rham-type theories need overconvergent/dagger variants. The thread is dropped at once.
missed.quote: il y a lieu de se poser la question de la validité de la conjecture faite ci-dessus, pour les [-espaces rigides-analytiques de Tate sur k-] ... espaces analytiques "flasques" sur k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a 1967 pointer to infinitesimal/stratified cohomology in rigid geometry, which was developed only much later (Berthelot, Grosse-Klönne, Guo). It is historically interesting as an early hint that Tate spaces alone are not the right category. Mathematically, the content is a question rather than a result.

deep.surprise_reason: The main statement is a routine reformulation (nilpotent invariance). The rigid-analytic remark is a fleeting, abandoned question whose 'flasque' qualifier is suggestive but unexplained, so it is mildly interesting historically and not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'Y de prés. finie sur S' (the object is Y, not F); 'on trouve' is likely 'on trouve' / 'on doit avoir'.
The site subscript is likely 'strat' (X_strat, X_0 strat), not 'fl'.
The line after 'flasques' sur k is likely 'Mais cela n'amène pas d'indications globales si remarquables ....', not 'n'avance pas d'induction globale'.
'Remarque' is underlined; the crossed-out text includes 'espaces rigides-analytiques de Tate sur k' and 'et rigides, mais en ...'.
